Title: The Effects of a Weight Loss Program Focusing on Maternal Education on Childhood Obesity
Author: Kang, Ryu, and Park
Comment: The endpoint mean difference was derived as control minus intervention: 84.88 - 83.62 = 1.26 cm, so a positive value favors intervention under the synthesis convention. SE_diff was derived from the explicitly reported endpoint SDs and group sizes as sqrt(7.64^2/32 + 6.73^2/33) = 1.7879 cm. These are unadjusted endpoint statistics; the reported F=18.98 is from an ANCOVA adjusting post-test for pre-test, but adjusted means, degrees of freedom, and an adjusted mean difference were not reported. The paper reports only p<.001, so no exact numeric p value was entered. The anatomical site for abdominal circumference was not specified.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Experimental group: child weight-control activities plus maternal-education intervention') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Randomized two-group pre-test/post-test controlled trial with ANCOVA adjustment for baseline
Medium: One maternal group-education session, three telephone-counseling contacts, and four informational fliers, added to child group education, self-monitoring, and a weight-control video
Topic of Content: Childhood obesity management, diet, exercise, behavior modification, and parental roles in child weight control
interaction_type: Maternal group education, telephone counseling, and mailed informational fliers
Participant type: Obese fourth- to sixth-grade elementary-school children and their mothers
Recruitment source: Fourth- to sixth-grade students at one elementary school in Incheon selected from the 2006 health examination
Outcome measurement: Tape-measured abdominal circumference; three measurements were averaged; anatomical measurement site was not reported

Title: Outcomes of a 1-year randomized controlled trial to evaluate a behavioral ‘stepped-down’ weight loss intervention for adolescent patients with obesity
Author: Norman et al.
Comment: The paper reports waist-circumference endpoint estimated marginal means and group × time P-values separately for girls and boys, but no combined-sex endpoint estimate or treatment effect. Because this extraction contract pre-identifies one study × outcome × comparison row and the schema cannot represent both sex strata in one row, subgroup means and P-values are preserved verbatim in the evidence quote but not entered into single-value numeric fields. Final analyzed Ns and SDs/SEs are not explicitly reported. No overall mean difference or SE can be validly computed. Eligibility as a technology-assisted intervention may require review adjudication because the digital element was limited: logs could be emailed or mailed, while much of the intervention was delivered in person, by telephone, and by post.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Stepped-down care (SDC)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); ANOVA excluded: comparison_type='mixed' is not between-group
Design Type: One-year two-arm parallel randomized controlled trial with repeated measures; sex-stratified mixed linear models
Study Environment: Three primary-care sites of the Children’s Primary Care Medical Group in Chula Vista, California; outcome assessments at the UCSD General Clinical Research Center
Medium: In-person and telephone health-educator counseling, mailed educational materials, self-monitoring logs that could be emailed or mailed, and pedometer, alongside primary-care counseling
Topic of Content: Adolescent obesity, diet, physical activity, and weight management
interaction_type: Clinician/health-educator counseling in person and by telephone, with mailed content and optional email or mail submission of self-monitoring logs for feedback
Participant type: Adolescents aged 11–13 years with obesity (BMI >95th percentile for age and gender)
Recruitment source: Primary-care clinics in San Diego County, primarily through pediatrician recommendation during routine care visits, with waiting-room flyers and physician-generated letters
Outcome measurement: Iliac waist circumference, average of two measurements by research staff following standardized procedures

Title: Lifestyle Intervention Using an Internet-Based Curriculum with Cell Phone Reminders for Obese Chinese Teens: A Randomized Controlled Study
Author: Abraham et al.
Comment: The paper reports medians and IQRs rather than means and SDs, so a mean difference and SE cannot be extracted or validly computed. The reported p = 0.065 is the Kruskal–Wallis endpoint comparison across all three groups (control, IT, and sLMP), not a direct IT-versus-control p value. The non-digital sLMP arm was excluded from the planned treatment comparison but is recorded in additional_group_ns.; mean/SD estimated from median/IQR via Wan et al. (2014): treatment mean=95.5750 SD=6.9090, control mean=101.1500 SD=11.7046 -- APPROXIMATION, not directly reported
Design Type: Three-arm randomized controlled pilot feasibility study with repeated measurements over 24 weeks
domain: Pediatric obesity and digital health/lifestyle intervention
Study Environment: Paediatric Obesity and Lipid Clinic at a tertiary care hospital
Medium: Internet-based curriculum with SMS/WhatsApp cell-phone reminders and follow-up
Content length: 12-week internet curriculum with cell-phone follow-up over 24 weeks
Topic of Content: Nutrition, physical activity, stress/coping, screen time, and healthy lifestyle for obesity management
interaction_type: Interactive online lessons, monthly diet and physical-activity goal setting, and weekly semi-personalized cell-phone messages
Participant type: Obese Chinese adolescents aged 12 to 18 years
Recruitment source: Paediatric Obesity and Lipid Clinic at a tertiary care hospital in Hong Kong
Outcome measurement: Waist circumference at week 24; measurement site and detailed protocol were not reported in the supplied text.
